style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind farm shed boss showing a kid the ropes.
lines: I'm Gus. Every order goes in one carton with no empty cups. Drag the carton's edge to change the rows.
That one fits, so it goes on the shelf. Try other rows to find every shape.
That's a carton you already have, just turned. Once the rows pass the columns, every fit is a turn.
That's every carton. More than one shape, so it's composite.
Only one long row fits. That order is prime.
One egg, one cup. One has just one factor, so it's neither prime nor composite.
Pick a carton size, then tap Run the line. If the last carton fills up, it's a multiple.
Every carton is full. It's a multiple of that size.
The last carton has empty cups. Not a multiple.
Every order you finish colors its number. Tap a number to pack it.
Rush orders get harder each shift. Read the card, then work it out.
Set the rows and tap Pack. When the shelf has every shape, tap Ship it.
Tap an order to load it. Then tap its crate. Composite needs a carton that proves it.
Pack a fitting carton with at least two rows and two columns first.
Turn on each size that fills with no gaps, type how many cartons, then tap Ship it.
Mark every order that only fits one long row, then tap Ship it.
Shipped. Right on time.
Not every shape yet. Try the rows you skipped.
Odd doesn't mean prime. One of those has another carton. Try more rows.
Two only fits one long row. It's the one even prime.
Only one goes in Neither. It has just one factor.
One size is off. Think about the last carton for each.
The sizes are right. Check how many cartons.
You missed one that only fits a long row.
Not quite. Check each order again.
Here's how I'd pack it. Watch.
Shift done. The truck's loaded.
